summary:
Custody placement is the sharpest documented exposure for a trans visitor. German prisons operate under statutory separation with a binary men and women housing model, and placement corresponding to a prisoner's gender identity has been practised only in exceptional cases; the Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony gives that reading of § 170(2) of the Lower Saxony correctional act as the operating rule and runs a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison. Several states have amended their prison statutes in recent years to accommodate legally recognised gender diversity, and a new § 17 of the Rhineland-Palatinate prison act took effect on 1 March 2026 with no press coverage at all.

How the exception is applied in practice remains unsettled. In August 2025 the chief prosecutor for Halle stated that Marla-Svenja Liebich, whose gender entry was changed to female at the end of 2024 under the Self-Determination Act, would serve an 18-month sentence for incitement at Chemnitz women's prison with placement reviewed at intake. After her extradition from Czechia in July 2026 she was transferred to a men's prison despite being legally registered as a woman since 2025; authorities cited the safety of prisoners at the women's facility, and critics called the gender change an abuse of the self-determination law.

DW reported on 23 August 2023 that German prisons offer few safe spaces for trans inmates, a finding illustrated by the case of climate activist Penelope Frank of Last Generation, legally recorded male, who faced assignment to a men's prison if convicted. The Berlin prison service maintains an official page in German with information and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary persons held across the city's facilities.

Screening is a documented flashpoint. In June 2025 the DJ and producer BASHKKA filed a legal complaint under Germany's Equal Treatment Act over a screening at Frankfurt Airport on 23 November 2024, in which officers allegedly deliberately disregarded her gender identity; she characterised the incident as a targeted, degrading act of transphobic harassment and gave Resident Advisor a copy of her statement to the airport.

Access to women-protected facilities has been contested since the Self-Determination Act took effect on 1 January 2025. A Deutscher Sauna-Bund guideline issued in January 2025 restricting women's saunas to persons whose primary sex characteristics correspond set off a debate about registered trans women's access, in which trans woman Alessia Dorigo argued that claiming a trans identity on a whim is unrealistic. Tagesspiegel Queerspiegel reported on how Berlin saunas and similar venues now treat trans women, after months of public argument over women-protected spaces and fears that the self-declaration route would be misused.

Reporting and support machinery exists for hostility encountered in country. The STOP the HATE campaign site, run by the Prevention and Empowerment organisation in northern Germany, provides a counselling finder sorted by topic, emergency guidance including an LSBTIQ* crisis line, and a hate-crime knowledge base covering underreporting, evidence preservation, witness support and reporting channels.
tangentialFactors:
Federal posture moved in a restrictive direction during 2025. In June the Federal Cabinet proposed designating Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia safe countries of origin despite LGBTI people facing imprisonment there; in July the Education Minister banned gender-inclusive language in her ministry, a step the Federal Anti-Discrimination Office said contradicts constitutional equality protection; in August the Merz coalition announced that it would end humanitarian admission programmes including the Afghanistan scheme for persecuted LGBTI people.

A March 2026 Verfassungsblog essay, Selbstbestimmung hinter Gittern, argues that trans prisoners need no discriminatory special law and that ordinary anti-discrimination law should govern their placement and treatment. The position treats the current patchwork of state prison statutes as the wrong instrument rather than a sufficient one.
localsOnly:
The prison-statute amendments of recent years, including the new § 17 in Rhineland-Palatinate, govern residents in custody rather than visitors, as does the Berlin prison service's page setting out facility-level rules and contacts for trans, inter and non-binary detainees.

Humanitarian admission programmes, among them the Afghanistan scheme for persecuted LGBTI people, were announced for closure in August 2025; these affect residents and asylum applicants, not short-term entry.

The ban on gender-inclusive language applies inside the Education Minister's ministry from July 2025, and the Federal Anti-Discrimination Office has stated that it contradicts constitutional equality protection. Its reach is public administration and residents.

The Criminological Research Institute of Lower Saxony maintains a research project on the situation of transgender people in prison, whose subject is conditions for residents in custody.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether identity-based placement is applied uniformly across the 16 states is unresolved in these sources. No national figure for the number of trans prisoners, and no data on the outcomes of intake placement reviews, is sourced here.

The legal weight of the Deutscher Sauna-Bund guideline against the Self-Determination Act is unresolved. The sources document the debate and individual venue practice, but no court ruling on whether a private association may restrict women's saunas by sex characteristics is available.

The outcome of BASHKKA's complaint under the Equal Treatment Act is not sourced, and no source states whether Frankfurt Airport screening procedures were revised after 23 November 2024.

Whether a visitor's gender marker is checked at entry in general, as distinct from the documented airport incident, is not addressed by any source in this inventory.
